
  shhh turns what you meant into something your machine can run, and it does    
  that at four different sizes.                                                 
         
  USAGE  
         
    shhh [command] [--flags]  
            
  SESSIONS  
            
    chat [prompt] [--flags]            Start a conversation
    cmd [prompt] [--flags]             Generate one shell command
    code [command] [prompt] [--flags]  Start a coding agent session
           
  RECORDS  
           
    chats [command] [--flags]          Browse, resume and tidy saved chats
    history [command] [--flags]        Browse past prompts and generated commands
    logs [--flags]                     Print what a session wrote down when a request failed
    memory [command]                   Manage durable agent memories
    metrics [--flags]                  Show provider usage metrics
    observe [command] [--flags]        Show agent-session usage dashboards
    rate [--flags]                     Rate past commands
    reports [command] [--flags]        List the report pages sessions built
    snippets [command] [--flags]       Manage saved command snippets
    todo [command]                     List the project's backlog
         
  SETUP  
         
    completion <shell>                 Generate shell completion script
    config [command]                   View and edit configuration
    doctor [--flags]                   Check this machine's shhh setup
    eval [suite] [--flags]             Run a suite of coding tasks and report what the session did
    init [shell] [--flags]             Output shell integration snippet or scaffold project config
    mcp [command] [--flags]            Connect each MCP server a session here would use, and report it
    providers [command] [--flags]      List providers and check gateway profiles
    skills [command]                   List the skills a session here would load
    update [--flags]                   Check for a newer shhh and refresh the model data
         
  FLAGS  
         
    -h --help                          Help for shhh
    -v --version                       Version for shhh
